agent_output.affected_group: Noncitizen Visa Waiver Program (VWP) travelers applying for admission to the United States at land ports of entry (from Canada or Mexico); also CBP.
agent_output.change_summary: DHS/CBP interim final rule amends 8 CFR parts 103, 212, 217, and 286 to extend the Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) requirement to VWP travelers arriving at U.S. land ports of entry. Such travelers must obtain an ESTA travel authorization prior to applying for admission (instead of completing the paper Form I-94W at the border); travelers without a valid authorization are ineligible for admission under the VWP. The existing ESTA fee applies; the $6.00 I-94W fee at land borders continues. Rule published 2022-04-01, effective 2022-05-02; comments due 2022-05-02.

evidence.quote:
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is amending 
its regulations to require VWP travelers applying for admission at U.S. 
land ports of entry to receive a travel authorization via the 
Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA) from CBP prior to 
applying for admission to the United States.

Through this interim rule, 
instead of completing a paper Form I-94W at land ports of entry, VWP 
travelers must now provide this information electronically to CBP via 
ESTA.

A VWP traveler who does not have a valid travel authorization 
at the time he or she applies for admission to the United States at a 
land port of entry will be ineligible for admission under the VWP.

for noncitizens who 
intend to enter the United States under the Visa Waiver Program (VWP) 
at land ports of entry.
This rule will affect VWP travelers, CBP, and the public.

DATES: This rule is effective May 2, 2022. Comments must be received on 
or before May 2, 2022.
ACTION: Interim final rule; solicitation of comments.

this interim final rule expanding ESTA to VWP 
travelers arriving at land ports of entry will be effective 30 days 
after publication.

uncertainties: Interim final rule with 30-day delayed effective date (2022-05-02); comments solicited and provisions could later be revised.
Document does not state the operational date CBP would begin denying admission beyond the regulatory effective date.
Only lines 1-1050 of 1787 were read; cost/benefit tables and amendatory text not reviewed.
Fee amounts cited are pre-existing; separate future rule for the legislated $17 TPA fee is not part of this event.
